source_findings: tests/browser/data-guest-picker-driver.mjs:310-360: Chromium 155 source confirms GetBoxModel frame-to-viewport output and getNodeForLocation document-to-frame input. For the supported scale=zoom=1, offset=0 case, measured cssLayoutViewport.pageY 479 plus box y66.5 yields hit y546 while mouse remains viewport y66.5. Browser.getVersion and getLayoutMetrics are captured before hit.

The shared clickPickerButton is called by Done, Cancel and Clear. Done still compares the post-foreground backendNodeId to the original and all three require strict hit.backendNodeId equality before page.mouse.click. A mismatched or missing hit refuses input. Unsupported pinch scale, page zoom, visual offset, unequal layout/visual pages, or missing zoom refuse before hit and click.

The hosted567 evidence recorded scrollY479 and viewport box center 41.8359375,66.5 with no_node before mouse; it did not record cssLayoutViewport, cssVisualViewport, Chrome version, or a corrected live hit. Source supports the repair but does not establish the hosted browser meets the supported-metrics precondition or that the actual button is hit.

quality_findings.issue: The actual sender is called and its probe/mouse arguments are asserted, but each button has only one scroll value (Done479, Cancel218, Clear0). A sender that hardcodes a per-button document Y can pass. Repeat the same button at a second nonzero measured scroll and a zero-scroll control in the same forcing case; keep mismatch/no-click checks. No executed constant-return gut check or RED/GREEN is available under the Mac resource guard.

The CDP double grants backendNodeId74 exactly when the sender supplies the test's expected coordinate. This proves sender wiring, not Chromium hit semantics or product outcome. A guarded real-browser naturally scrolled picker must capture Browser version/layout metrics, exact same button hit, unchanged viewport trusted click, and Done result; Cancel/Clear need their product outcomes.
